textbookText: (b) Nematic crystals: (1) These have molecules parallel to each other and free to slide or roll individually (Greek: Nematic = thread). (2) They flow like normal liquids and flow readily than smectic liquid crystals. The flow of these liquid crystals obeys the Newtonian laws. Their viscosity is low as compared to liquids. (3) These are closer to true anisotropic liquids than smectic liquid crystals. They have low viscosity. (4) In polarized light they have mobile thread like structure. The molecules are aggregated together in groups or swarms with their axis parallel to one another. (5) In electric or magnetic field, the swarms of nematic liquid crystals are oriented in unique direction. (6) The turbidity of nematic crystals arises due to the scattering of light by these crystals. (7) Due to orientation of molecules about a preferred axis (director axis) nematic state shows anisotropy in optical, diamagnetic, elastic properties etc. e.g. p- azoxy phenetole, p-azoxy anisole, dibenzal benzidine etc.

(c) Chloesteric liquid crystals: In these crystals, the molecules are arranged parallel in the form of layers. The molecules in successive layers are slightly rotated with the layers above and below forming a spiral structure. They exhibit very high optical rotatory power. The pitch of spiral and reflected color depends on temperature. They are named as chloesteric crystals because the skeleton of substance passing through this state is as like that of cholesterol. Chloesteric liquid crystals have some smectic and some nematic characters. e.g. cholesteryl benzoate (m.p. = 178 oC, transition point = 145 oC).

1. Liquid crystal displays are common in calculators, digital watches, television displays using L.C. screens has also been developed. Cholesteric liquid crystals have also been used for novelty items such as toys and decorative materials. 2.liquid crystals are widely used in cosmetic industry in manufacturing of liquid crystal makeup removers, lipsticks and lip glasses containing cholesteric liquid crystals. 3.
